title: compact-oncall-breadcrumbs-and-rollback-hint-proxy
author: Maya Chen
description: Summary: Adds a lightweight on-call 'breadcrumbs' capture and a small rollback-hint proxy that surfaces likely revert actions when automated mitigations are suggested. Motivation: during incidents engineers wanted a compact, privacy-safe timeline that highlights key actions (deploys, autoscale events, mitigation commands) without pulling full traces or huge logs. This PR implements a compact breadcrumb store, a UI card to surface breadcrumbs in the incident view, and a small proxy that annotates runbook suggestions with a 'rollback hint' when the recent breadcrumb pattern matches known deploy-caused incidents. Design notes: - Breadcrumbs are sampled, encrypted at rest, and kept for 7 days by default. Each breadcrumb is a small structured event (type, short message, actor, timestamp, optional anchor token) limited to 256 bytes to avoid PII. - Rollback-hint proxy is a ruleset-based annotator that consults recent breadcrumbs and the incident's signal taxonomy to append a hint like: "recent deploy from service-x at 03:14 may be a root cause — consider revert or pin previous image". Rules are conservative and require two corroborating signals to avoid noisy suggestions. - Privacy sanitization: breadcrumb messages go through a sanitizer that strips emails, long stack traces, and API keys. The UI shows a blurred preview with an expand action that requires an extra click and an audit log entry. - Backwards compatibility: feature guarded behind a config flag incident_bot.features.breadcrumbs and an RBAC toggle (role: incident_reader or higher). No API changes for existing webhooks. Checklist: - [x] Implement breadcrumb collector and in-memory sharded store - [x] Persist compact snapshots to object store with TTL - [x] Add sanitizer and redact pipeline - [x] Rollback-hint proxy with 3 simple rules + unit tests - [x] UI card component with blur/expand and audit hook - [x] Helm values and upgrade docs - [x] End-to-end smoke test in CI (local emulation) What changed (high level): commits: see commits list; files changed: internal oncall capture, sanitizer, annotator, small web UI component, helm values, docs. Testing: unit tests for capture rules and rollback proxy rules; an integration smoke harness that simulates a deploy->latency spike pattern and verifies hint shows up. CI notes: initial CI run had a flaky snapshot test (tests/oncall/breadcrumbs_test.go TestSanitizerRace) that failed on race on macOS runners; I reproduced locally, added a short mutex around the test harness and re-ran — CI passed on rerun. Rollout: behind config flag; we'll flip in a controlled canary group (10% of orgs) for 48 hours then widen. If we see more than 3 false-positive hints per 100 incidents, we will rollback the flag. Related work: ENG-2184 (compact incident artifacts), ENG-3301 (runbook hinting RFC). Docs: docs/runbooks/breadcrumbs.md explains storage, retention, and administrator controls. Links: design RFC: https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-2184/compact-breadcrumbs, deploy checklist: https://wiki.redwood.internal/oncall/breadcrumbs-deploy. Release notes: Adds optional breadcrumbs capture and rollback hinting to incident-bot behind feature flag. No breaking changes. Security: breadcrumbs sanitized and encrypted; KMS-integration for object store snapshots documented.

ci_summary: Initial CI run: unit tests 152 passed, 1 flaky failure (sanitizer race) on macOS runner; re-run succeeded. Integration smoke passed in emulation. Lint and security scans pass.
release_notes: Adds opt-in lightweight breadcrumbs capture for incidents and a conservative rollback-hint annotator. Feature is disabled by default; ops can enable via incident_bot.features.breadcrumbs in helm values. Sanitization and audit controls included.
notes_for_ops: After upgrade: set incident_bot.features.breadcrumbs=true and tune incident_bot.breadcrumbs.ttl_days to desired retention. Monitor metric oncall.breadcrumbs.sanitizer_rejects and oncall.breadcrumbs.hints_true_positives/false_positives.
deploy_plan: Canary enable for 10% orgs for 48h, monitor false-positive rate and sanitizer reject counts; rollback by setting flag to false and deleting recent compact snapshots if privacy concerns arise.
